Brother, is the announcement of the same happy event to near relatives and friends who would be naturally more or less acquainted with the ups and downs that poor dear Father Maurice was known to have gone through, and the more than ordinary disappointments, humiliations, ambitions and sometimes triumphs of his over 81 years. Even among such near and dear ones, however, -- though the ideal seems to be common in the "Island of Saints" -- comparatively few ever knew of the fact that our dear Parents had mutually dreamed of the privilege of being parent to a Priest in their family, which ideal would seem to have buoyed their hopes from the earliest years wherein they recognized holy matrimony as a state of life in which to serve God and help Him to save souls. Furthermore; when the writer was in his seventh year and there were three brothers among the five dear-ones ahead of him, it just seemed self - understood as though planned before his birth that Maurice was to be the Priest. Not only was this the case in our immediate family and relatives, but our neighboring children often spoke of it and seemed to revere him as so fortunately destined and chosen. So much was this true that some one even at that time and perhaps earlier, began to wonder if possibly there couldn't be two priests in a family -- hardly hesitating that he would be the other himself. However, promising and all as was his childhood and early youth to harmonize with such happy plannings, the old proverb
